newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols steady ahead of refunding.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols steady ahead of refunding.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were generally steady to softer in quiet trading as the market awaited the Treasury's refunding auctions and Tuesday's U.S. elections, dealers said.
"I've seen a few 500-lot trades, but it's been very quiet," said a Treasury bond trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Board of Trade.

He said volatilities were still perceived to be relatively rich after getting pumped up before last Friday's October U.S. employment report, although they have come down significantly since Friday morning when the jobs data came out.
Implied volatility for March T-bond futures options stood at around 10.0 percent, virtually unchanged from Friday's closing levels.
Traders said they had so far seen little hedging activity by auction participants, partly because the underlying market looked resilient despite the supply concerns.
December T-bond futures were up 8/32 at 113-00 in early afternoon trade.
The Treasury is due to auction $18.5 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday, $10 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and $10 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday.
Traders expected the market would have little trouble absorbing the new issues and would resume its recent uptrend before long.
October producer and consumer prices data are due for release on November 13 and 14 respectively.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, volatilities for Eurodollar futures options were a touch softer.

Growing expectations that the Federal Reserve would not change interest rates for a while were dampening movement in futures, prompting selling in options, traders said. March Eurodollar futures were up one basis point to 94.43.
"They (volatilities) got hit hard on Friday and I think there's a little bit of followthrough on that," said a trader for an investment bank at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Implied volatility for March Eurodollar futures options was off 0.2 point on the day to about 13.5 percent.
